subject: Performance degradation in Brightline reserved pool — initial triage and next steps
body:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightline.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected inference slowness - reserved pool degrading

Hi Priyom,

We're seeing a sudden increase in p99 latency and a backlog in our reserved pool jobs since ~08:30 PT. Jobs that usually finish in 3–4s are taking 20–40s and some are timing out. The dashboard shows queue length spiking and several GPU nodes reporting OOM/eviction events.

Can you confirm whether there's any ongoing maintenance or known issues on the Dedicated pools for our US-east cluster? I've attached the tail of our job runner logs and a short capture of the metrics dashboard.

Attachments: brightline_prod_logs_0907.tar.gz (logs, 12MB)

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior SRE, Brightline AI

---

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected inference slowness - reserved pool degrading

Hi Jordan — thanks for the quick heads up and for sending the logs. We're not running any scheduled maintenance in your region. I'm escalating to infra on-call (copying Sean) and asking for an immediate triage.

Immediate plan:
- We'll pull the attached logs into the diagnostics channel and look for OOM / eviction patterns.
- If a single service/process is leaking memory we'll orchestrate a rolling restart to avoid a full pool outage.
- I'll propose a 30-minute maintenance window if we need to roll nodes.

Can you confirm a 30-min window between 11:00–12:00 PT if we need to perform rolling restarts? Also please share any customer-facing SLAs impacted so we can scope credits if applicable.

I've attached a short diagnostic checklist for a few extra traces we might ask you for.
Attachments: diagnostic-request.txt

— Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

---

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Brightline incident initial triage (private)

Short summary (for the thread):
- Symptom: sudden p99 latency increase, queue backlog, node OOM events in Brightline reserved pool (us-east).
- Evidence: customer logs + our node telemetry show steady increase in GPU-process RSS and fragmentation; several kernels report failed allocations preceding OOM.
- Hypothesis: a memory leak introduced in runtime build rwinf-2.9.1 (deployed 2026-09-06) causing long-lived slot fragmentation; autoscaler mis-evaluated available capacity, leading to scheduling contention and transient throttling rather than scale-up.

Actions taken so far:
1) Scoped the affected fleet subset (reserved pool group RP-128-east) and blocked new job placements to prevent further contention.
2) Collected heap dumps from two representative nodes — saved as heap-dump-20260907.bin.
3) Performed a targeted rolling restart of 20% of nodes at 10:20 PT; observed immediate drop in queue length and partial recovery.
4) PUT in motion a hotfix rollout to address allocator regression; CI-green for rwinf-2.9.2 build at 10:40 PT.

Customer comms plan (to send after internal agreement):
- Notify customer of root cause hypothesis (memory leak in runtime), immediate remediation done (rolling restarts + hotfix staging), and proposed permanent fix (hotfix rollout + additional telemetry and an autoscaler patch).
- Offer one month of service credit proportional to observed throttling window.
- Share draft postmortem + timelines for follow-up.

Attachments: heap-dump-20260907.bin (internal artifact)

Please review and add anything I missed. We should finalize external wording before sending.

— Priyom

---

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightline.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kerry O'Connor <kerry.oconnor@brightline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected inference slowness - reserved pool degrading

Thanks — that matches what we're seeing on our side. The 11:00–11:30 PT window works for us for the rolling restarts. Appreciate the quick containment; can you confirm timing for the hotfix rollout and the bandwidth of the service credit you're proposing? We had several client jobs impacted (roughly 1.2K inference calls during the spike window).

Also, please send the postmortem draft when available — our compliance team will want the timeline.

Jordan

---

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2026 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Brightline reserved pool degradation — mitigation complete and postmortem link

Hi Jordan,

Follow-up from our side — mitigation is complete and we've rolled the rwinf-2.9.2 hotfix to your reserved pool (completed 2026-09-08 03:20 PT). Summary:
- Root cause: regression in memory allocator in rwinf-2.9.1 causing gradual GPU-process memory growth and slot fragmentation; autoscaler heuristics did not trigger aggressive scale-up because free contiguous slot estimation underreported fragmentation.
- Immediate mitigation: targeted rolling restarts reduced queue length and restored baseline latency by ~90% within 30 minutes. Hotfix rollout replaced the allocator and added an allocation-failure counter metric to detect recurrence.
- Long-term mitigations: autoscaler patch to consider fragmentation metrics, additional leak detection alerts, and a scheduled canary rollout for runtime updates.

We've prepared a short draft postmortem for your review: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/INC-20260907-brightline (read-only). The draft includes timeline, root cause analysis, remediation steps, and proposed credits. A copy is also in our shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4-postmortem-brightline

Credits: as a gesture for the disruption during the spike window (09:00–10:00 PT on 2026-09-07) we're proposing a one-month credit equivalent to the usage-based charges attributable to the impacted tokens/requests; Marissa (cc'd) will follow up with the formal billing adjustment and calculation.

Next steps:
- Marissa to send formal credit breakdown and timing.
- We'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the postmortem and the autoscaler patch next week — propose Tue 2026-09-14 10:00 PT; please confirm availability.
- We'll keep the postmortem draft editable for 72 hours for any corrections or additional customer context.

Apologies again for the disruption — we know this impacted production jobs and are treating the reliability improvements as a priority. Thanks for the prompt cooperation during containment.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference
